body.statement: Under perfect compliance, \(D_{ni}(0)=0\) and \(D_{ni}(1)=1\), and universal selection, \(S_{ni}(0)=S_{ni}(1)=1\), one has \(\ell_{n,x,k}=f_{1,n,x,k}\), \(h_{n,x,k}=f_{0,n,x,k}\), \(w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}(f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), and \(M_n=1\). Consequently \(\Theta_{I,n}=[\sum_x p_{n,x}b_L((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}),\sum_x p_{n,x}b_U((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime})]\), the covariate-stratified ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds; without covariate stratification these are the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta bounds.
body.justification: This reduction checks that the selected-complier capacity formulas collapse to the established ordinal-benefit geometry when compliance and observability cease to be latent.
body.gap: Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta establish the ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds; this proposition is a required reduction, not a novelty claim.
body.consumer: It gives implementers an exact benchmark for validating the capacity and min-cut code against standard two-arm ordinal data.
